chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khathʿami, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Do not say “Ramadan”, but say “the Month of Ramadan”, for you do not know what Ramadan is.’

key_terms.رَمَضَان: The name of the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, the month of fasting; its full Quranic form is ‘Shahr Ramadan’
key_terms.شَهْر: Month; the proper qualifier that must accompany the name ‘Ramadan’ according to this teaching
key_terms.صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: Blessings of God be upon him — a salutation used specifically for Imam Ali (AS) in Shia tradition

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Ali say to say ‘Month of Ramadan’ instead of just ‘Ramadan’?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmitted this instruction from Imam Ali (AS), the Commander of the Faithful, forbidding the use of the bare name ‘Ramadan’ without the qualifier ‘month’ (shahr). The theological reason given is that the true nature and significance of Ramadan is beyond human comprehension, so the proper designation ‘Shahr Ramadan’ — as used in the Quran — should be maintained out of reverence and epistemic humility. This hadith reflects the Shia jurisprudential concern with preserving the sanctity of Quranic terminology.
